title: fix(memory): measure view merge age from the pair last message
description: view.go:149-151 computes due = (tailTo - start)/2^(level+2) using a.Range() start, i.e. the pair FIRST message. The optchat spec says this is the buggy first version (the 2^2 changes nothing; the bug was first). It merges old pairs at ties and churns old lines. Reproduced with a temporary test at the spec T=10 case: golem merges 0-7 instead of the newest 8-9.
design: Use due = (tailTo - last)/2^level where last is the pair last message (second part Range end minus 1), equivalently (tailTo+1)/2^level - index. Drop the +2 weight. Keep the built-parent gate and oldest-of-equal tie-break.
acceptance_criteria: A unit test reproduces the spec T=10 view (parts 0+4, 4+4, 8+1, 9+1, tailTo=10) and asserts the newest pair (level0 8,9 into level1 index4) merges, not 0-7. Existing view and compactor tests pass under -race.
close_reason: Merge age now measured from the pair end (OptChat 3.2); bestMergeIndex extracted and regression test TestViewMergeOrderMeasuresFromPairEnd added; fractal tests pass under -race.

title: fix(memory): render live-head recent events into the main agent prompt
description: The main agent never sees the newest raw events. RenderCombined (pkg/memory/fractal/multi_store.go:179) renders only View.Render(), which excludes the newest LiveHeadCount (10) events (view.go:208). Only the subagent MemoryContext (pkg/golem/agent.go:488-508) and the TUI cockpit call LiveHeadEvents(). The main InstructionProvider (agent.go:527-580) calls RenderCombined only. Combined with IncludeContentsNone and a fresh session per turn (agent.go:526,763), the model sees the current message plus coarse summaries but not the immediately preceding exchange. A short turn (user+reply) leaves the next view empty.
design: Append view.LiveHeadEvents() formatted like the subagent path (agent.go:488) after RenderCombined in the InstructionProvider. Prefer a shared renderLiveHead helper used by both main and subagent paths. Ensure the current user message is not duplicated; consider raising DefaultLiveHeadCount and the 120-char per-event truncation.
acceptance_criteria: The InstructionProvider output contains the most recent raw events (id, kind, truncated text) in a dedicated block. A pkg/golem test seeds user/talk/tool events within the live-head window, renders the instruction via the provider, and asserts the recent user turn appears; after a second turn with fewer than LiveHeadCount intervening events the prior exchange is still visible verbatim. -race passes.
close_reason: Extracted buildInstruction/formatLiveHead and inject a bounded recent_live_head block into the main agent prompt (subagent path reuses it). In-flight user message is dropped to avoid duplication. Added TestBuildInstructionIncludesLiveHead and TestFormatLiveHeadBoundsAndKeepsNewest; pkg/golem tests pass under -race.

title: Fractal memory rapid-forgetting: restore short-term context and fix the view algorithm
description:
Audit found that Golem loses recent context (moves short-term into long-term far too fast) and mis-locates itself across sessions/repos. Four root causes confirmed by reading the code and reproducing the merge order against the real fitLocked:

1. The main agent prompt never renders the live head. RenderCombined (pkg/memory/fractal/multi_store.go:179) renders only View.Render(), which excludes the newest LiveHeadCount (10) events. Only the subagent path (pkg/golem/agent.go:488) and the TUI cockpit consume LiveHeadEvents(). With IncludeContentsNone and a fresh session per turn (agent.go:526,763), the model sees the current message plus coarse summaries, but not the immediately preceding exchange. Short turns leave the view empty.

2. The merge-age formula measures from the pair first message, the exact bug the optchat spec warns against. view.go:149-151 computes due = (tailTo - start)/2^(level+2). Reproduced against fitLocked at the spec T=10 case: it merges the oldest pair 0-7 instead of the newest 8-9.

3. Merges run on every event with no low-water mark. fitLocked merges until size <= 128000 and is called after every append (view.go:117-121,128). The spec batches from 128 KB down to 64 KB; golem pins the view at the ceiling and can cascade-coarsen recent lines on every tool/echo event.

4. Overlong summaries are silently truncated (compactor.go:80,146) instead of retried, and the claimed 512-byte ruler is actually 505 bytes (compactor.go:26).

Outcome: recent raw events are always in context; the view coarsens in the correct order and only in batches; summaries are not silently clipped; the view survives restart.
design: Fix order: (1) live-head injection (biggest user-visible win), (2) merge-age formula, (3) batching+low-water, (4) view persistence, (5) summary retry+ruler. Each fix ships with a regression test. Finish with an adversarial code review.

title: Repair tool arguments a model typed as strings
description: Models sometimes send a number as a JSON string: zoom called as {"id":"5441","n":"1"} was rejected by the ADK's schema validation before the handler ran ("validating /properties/id: type: 5441 has type \"string\", want \"integer\""), so the call was lost and the model, never told why, repeated it until the turn was interrupted.
design: The tool's own declaration already says which arguments are integers, numbers or booleans, so the repair is schema-driven and shared: tools.RepairArgs walks the declaration schema and coerces only stringified literals of those types, descending into object parameters. String parameters are untouched, so a shell command or file name that looks like a number stays a string; unparseable values are left for the tool's own error. It runs as the first BeforeToolCallback of the orchestrator and of every subagent, which works because the args map handed to a callback is the same map handed to the tool.
acceptance_criteria: zoom/date calls with stringified integers run; string args unchanged; nested object numbers repaired; test fails without the callback (mutation-checked)
close_reason: tools.RepairArgs + repairToolArguments callback (orchestrator and subagents); tests: pkg/tools/args_test.go (stringified ints/bools/floats, nested objects, string args untouched, unparseable, no-schema) and pkg/golem/toolargs_test.go end-to-end zoom via ADK (fails without the callback); build/vet/test/-race green

title: Harden shell: working dir, env scrub, resource caps

design: cmd.Dir = workspace root from config. Build env from an allowlist (PATH, HOME, TERM, LANG, TMPDIR) instead of inheriting; explicitly drop *_API_KEY, *_TOKEN, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, AWS_*. Set Setpgid + kill the process group on timeout so children die. Optional rlimits via syscall.Setrlimit in a pre-exec (CPU, address space, file size, nproc). Make the timeout configurable per profile.
acceptance_criteria: A command cannot see credentials from the daemon environment (test asserts a known secret is absent from env output); relative paths resolve against the workspace not the daemon cwd; a timed-out command leaves no surviving children; rlimits are applied when configured.
close_reason: shell now runs in the workspace with the policy env allowlist, a policy timeout and a process-group kill; isolation mode also sets RLIMIT_CORE=0 and denies setuid via no_new_privs

title: Sandbox: policy layer (A) then OS isolation (B)
description:
pkg/tools/shell.go runs exec.CommandContext(ctx, 'bash', '-c', command) with a 120s timeout and no cmd.Dir, no env scrubbing and no network or filesystem restriction - anything the model writes runs as the user. File tools are already contained (file_editor.go:16-45 ErrPathOutOfBounds + filepath.Rel against a root) and pkg/web has an SSRF guard, so there is precedent for policy, just no general layer. There is no confirmation gate anywhere in pkg/.
Threat model agreed: A (contain accidents - rm -rf ~, git checkout .) and then B (contain a hostile or prompt-injected model via OS-level isolation). C (multi-tenant) is out of scope.
A is a prerequisite for the graph and web epics: once an agent can author a DAG that fans out 20 shell nodes, or a phone can drive it unattended, accidents become incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Every tool call in the process goes through one policy decision point; a profile can deny shell entirely, allow write only under the workspace, and require confirmation for shell; each transport renders the confirmation prompt; behaviour is covered by tests for allow, deny and confirm paths.
close_reason: sandbox epic complete: one policy point for every tool (9uw.1), Landlock isolation for the shell (9uw.2/.4), human approval gate across TUI/web/readline (9uw.3), audited decisions (9uw.5), /api/patch routed through policy (9uw.6), MCP toolsets gated+allowlisted (9uw.7). Known gaps tracked in golem-c8l.

title: pkg/sandbox: one policy decision point for all tools
description: There is no shared policy concept today: shell is unconstrained, file tools have their own private path checks, web_fetch has its own SSRF guard. Three ad-hoc policies and no place to put a fourth.
design: type Policy with Mode (off/policy/bwrap), AllowWrite, AllowNet, RequireConfirm, EnvAllow. type Decision {Verdict: allow|deny|confirm, Reason}. Methods: CheckShell(argv, dir), CheckWrite(path), CheckNet(url). Wire into shell.go, file_editor.go, hashline, web. Keep the existing path and SSRF checks as the innermost implementation so nothing regresses. Config parsing in pkg/config with sane defaults (mode: policy, allow_write: [workspace], require_confirm: [shell]).
acceptance_criteria: One constructor and one interface used by all four tool families; a single test table drives allow/deny for shell, write and net; mode off reproduces today's behaviour exactly; no tool can bypass the layer without a deliberate bypass call.
close_reason: pkg/sandbox policy layer wired into shell, file, hashline and web tools; config sandbox block; mode off reproduces old behaviour; table tests for allow/deny/confirm

title: Web cockpit usable from a phone over the tailnet
description:
ui/ is a full SvelteKit cockpit (sessions, ChatArea streaming, SwarmTree, MemoryExplorer, ProfileModal, PatchInspector) and ui/src/lib/client.ts derives the WS URL from window.location.host, so it already works through tailscale serve. pkg/server/static.go embeds the built SPA in the binary. What blocks real phone use is not features, it is hardening and layout:
  1. no auth of any kind - hub.go:13 CheckOrigin returns true, every /api/* is open, Addr ':8080' binds all interfaces (see golem-ppp). Any tailnet device gets an unconfined bash -c as the user.
  2. desktop-locked layout - h-screen w-screen, w-80 swarm sidebar, fixed w-[520px]/w-[540px] right drawers, h-12 header with six buttons. Overflows a 390px phone.
  3. reconnect loses streamed tokens - scheduleReconnect backs off to 15s but never resumes; mobile backgrounding kills the socket and the reply is gone.
  4. not installable - no manifest, no theme-color, no apple-mobile-web-app meta.
design:
No second mobile route: one responsive pass on +page.svelte, not a forked UI.
Auth: bearer token (generated once, persisted in ~/.golem/config.json, overridable with -token) required on /ws and /api/*; static assets exempt; constant-time compare; startup banner prints the full URL including token. Optional second factor: trust Tailscale-User-Login when present (set by tailscale serve).
Layout: drawers full-bleed below sm, sidebar behind a toggle, 100dvh + env(safe-area-inset-*), 16px minimum input font to stop iOS zoom-on-focus, 44px touch targets.
Resume: per-session monotonic seq + server-side ring buffer; client sends {resume:{session_id,last_seq}} on open and server replays; add read deadlines/pong handling alongside the existing 30s writePump ticker.
acceptance_criteria: Loading the UI from a phone over tailscale on a 390x844 viewport shows no horizontal scroll and every control reachable; /api/* and /ws reject unauthenticated requests with 401; killing the mobile browser and reopening resumes the in-flight reply without loss; the UI can be added to the home screen and launches standalone.

close_reason: buildInstruction/formatLiveHead now exclude every event with ID >= the turn start (not just the user message), so ongoing tool/echo chatter is not duplicated in the prompt. Updated TestBuildInstructionIncludesLiveHead.

title: feat(provider/openai): retry transient HTTP failures at the request level
description: The OpenAI-compatible client posts once with a 120s timeout and no retry, so transient 429/503/5xx/timeouts propagate to the turn loop and (with the old behavior) restart whole turns. Add bounded exponential backoff retry on 429/500/502/503/504 and network errors, honoring context cancellation and Retry-After. Gemini already has retry via genai ClientConfig.
acceptance_criteria: A request that fails transiently is retried up to a bound and succeeds without surfacing to the caller; permanent errors and cancellation are not retried; tests use an httptest server returning 503 then 200.
close_reason: Added doRequestWithRetry to the OpenAI-compatible client: bounded exponential backoff on 429/5xx and network errors, Retry-After honored, cancellation stops promptly. Tests: retries-then-succeeds, no-retry-on-400, cancellation.

title: Reduce wasteful spinning on simple tasks (harness efficiency)
description: Golem should be allowed to run long on hard tasks, but simple tasks spin. Audit found harness-side waste: (1) any transient error restarts the whole turn from zero, re-running every tool; (2) the OpenAI-compatible client has no per-request retry, so transient 429/503/timeouts reach the turn loop; (3) the live head re-injects the current turn events that are already in the conversation; (4) up to 128KB of global summary view is prefixed to every task; (5) the compactor competes for the same provider quota during a turn. Fixes target wasted work, not a time cap.
design: Progress-aware turn retry; HTTP retry in the provider client; exclude current-turn IDs from the live head; lower the default view budget; pause the compactor worker while a turn is active.
acceptance_criteria: A transient error after progress does not re-execute tools; per-request retry absorbs blips; simple-task prompts are smaller; compaction does not contend with an active turn; all with tests.
close_reason: Efficiency epic complete: turns never restart after progress or after text has been streamed, the provider retries transient failures per request (incl. 408), the live head excludes the current turn, compaction views are their own 16-32 KB window that ends at the node, compaction pauses during a turn, and the small view budget was measured (3.5 zooms/user message at 64 KB vs 0 at 128 KB) so the spec 128/64 KB default stands. Dead CompactorConfig.Concurrency removed.

title: fix(memory): batch view merges with a 64 KB low-water mark
description: fitLocked merges to the 128 KB ceiling after every appended event (view.go:117-121,128), so each new tool/echo event can trigger a cascade that coarsens recent lines. The spec batches: grow to 128 KB, then merge down to 64 KB once, and between batches the view only grows at its end.
design: Add LowWaterBytes (default 64000) to ViewConfig; keep ViewBudgetBytes as the high-water alias. fitLocked targets low-water and is only entered when size > high-water. Keep per-append Sync cheap.
acceptance_criteria: Merging runs only when size exceeds a high-water mark (default 128000) and merges down to a low-water mark (default 64000) in one batch. A test asserts a single append while under high-water performs no merge, and that after a batch the size is <= low-water. No old line churns between batches.
close_reason: View now batches: fitLocked is a no-op at/below the high-water mark and merges in one pass down to a configurable low-water mark (default high/2). Added TestViewBatchingRespectsHighAndLowWater; fractal tests pass under -race.

title: fix(memory): persist the view across restarts instead of rebuilding
description: NewView always calls Rebuild (view.go:76). The optchat spec lists rebuilding the view at restart as mistake #3: the rebuilt tiling can differ from the live one and re-coarsens detail, and it kills the prompt cache. There is no view persistence today (store has events, nodes, metadata buckets only).
design: Persist parts plus tailTo in a bbolt bucket keyed per store; validate on load against CountEvents and the configured LiveHeadCount. Update on Sync/batch merges, not on every event if that is expensive.
acceptance_criteria: The view tiling is saved after changes and loaded on OpenStore/NewView. A test creates a store+view, syncs, closes, reopens, and asserts the rendered view equals the pre-close render. Rebuild is a fallback only when no saved view exists or it is inconsistent with the event count.
close_reason: View tiling is now persisted to a bbolt view bucket and loaded on NewView; falls back to Rebuild only when absent/inconsistent. Added TestViewPersistsAcrossRestart; fractal tests pass under -race.

title: Swarm A: thread SubagentID back through InvokeResult so the orchestrator can address peers

The ID (subagent-<role>-<unixnano>) is generated inside Runner.Invoke and only whispered to the subagent via its system prompt, so the orchestrator can never actually address a running peer with send_message — the 'peer agents' story breaks at the ID round-trip. Add SubagentID to InvokeResult (and the subagent_done event), and surface it in the invoke_subagent tool result header so the orchestrator learns the ID. Part of Swarm lane A (wake it up).
close_reason: Added SubagentID to InvokeResult and Event; Runner.Invoke generates the id up front and sets it on every result + subagent_start/done events; invoke_subagent result header now reports 'id: <subagent-id>' so the orchestrator can address peers.

title: Graph runs get a durable ADK session so a paused node can resume across turns
description:
golem gives every turn a throwaway ADK session (turn-<nano> in pkg/golem/agent.go), and workflow.RunState is reconstructed from session history rather than from stored state (runner/run_node.go:182 ReconstructRunState). So a graph node that pauses (HITL RequestInput, long-running tool) currently has nowhere to resume from: a graph_run that pauses must either fail or be re-run from the start.

Design direction: give each graph run its own session id and drive it through a runner with a session.Service that outlives the process, so Resume(wf, ReconstructRunState(sess, invocationID), responses) works on a later turn. Options: (a) implement a small JSON-file session.Service in pkg/graph (events+state per session, ~250 lines, no new deps); (b) session/database (gorm dialector, needs SQLite driver); (c) back it with the fractal store that already persists events. Then graph_run returns a run id, graph_resume(name, run_id, responses) answers the pending node, and graph_status lists paused runs.

Acceptance: a graph whose node calls a require_confirm tool pauses, survives a golem restart, and resumes with a 'yes' on the next turn; the resumed run does not re-execute completed nodes.
notes: Starting point: pkg/graph/run.go drive() already wraps the workflow in agent.New and runs it through a per-run runner with session.InMemoryService + AutoCreateSession, then deletes the session. Making that service durable (file or database backed) plus keeping the session id in the spec/run record is most of the work; Resume() then takes ReconstructRunState(sess, invocationID). Note that runner/run_node.go's HITL path (RequestInputEvent/ResumeOrRequestInput) is already wired inside the workflow engine, so a node that pauses should need no new machinery beyond the durable session and a graph_resume tool.
close_reason: Landed: fileSessionService (JSONL events + state per run under .golem/graphs/runs/<id>/session), RunRecord + graph_stat/graph_resume, graph nodes now get interactive tools so a gated call pauses the run, approval wrapper (pkg/graph/approval.go) makes the human's answer effective on resume. Verified live: gate graph paused on shell require_confirm, graph_resume approve=true ran it, run completed; 4 new tests incl. restart survival.

title: Per-session UI state in the TUI Model

Move everything conversation-scoped out of Model into chatState; keep chrome (size, theme, modals, spinner) on Model. Commands that touch the agent take the active session id explicitly so a late-arriving message cannot land in the wrong session - tag streamed messages with their session id.

title: Multi-session TUI over a shared runtime
description:
pkg/server/session_manager.go already solved multi-session for the web UI: per-session golem.Agent with isolated StorageDir/<session-id> (:65-67), TryAcquireTurn, ListSessions/SetActiveSession/ActiveSession, owned by server.go:77. The TUI has none of it: main.go:312 constructs the agent before the TUI exists and tui.NewModel(agent, store, view) at :358, with Model holding a single agent, a single entries slice and a single viewport (model.go:120-161).
So the work is mostly extraction, not invention - and the same extraction is what the web epic and any future transport need.
design:
Lift SessionManager out of pkg/server into a UI-agnostic pkg/runtime. A Session owns {agent, store, view, compactor, swarmBus, ctx} and can be suspended (close bbolt, stop the compactor goroutine) and resumed. pkg/server becomes one consumer of pkg/runtime; the TUI becomes a second.
bbolt is single-writer with a 5s open timeout (store.go:81), so N live sessions means N open DBs and N compactor workers: lazy-load on switch, suspend after idle (~5 min), never point two processes at one memory dir.
acceptance_criteria: TUI can hold several sessions, switch between them without losing scroll position or draft, and close them; pkg/server keeps working unchanged through the same runtime; idle sessions release their bbolt handle.
close_reason: Closed

title: Persist graph specs and per-session RunState
description: Workflow objects are not serialisable, and RunState is the only thing that survives a turn boundary. Nothing persists graphs today.
design: Specs in ~/.golem/graphs/<name>.json (0600, human-editable, git-friendly). RunState keyed per session AND per graph name in the session state so a paused graph resumes on the next user turn; namespace the workflow name as <session>/<graph> to avoid the silent-overwrite trap. On load: read spec, re-validate, rebuild the Workflow. Deleting a graph must not orphan an in-flight run - refuse or mark it cancelled.
acceptance_criteria: A graph created in one turn can be resumed in a later turn and after a process restart; two sessions can run same-named graphs without interfering; a spec edited on disk is re-validated before use; an invalid on-disk spec fails loudly rather than silently disappearing.
notes: PARTIAL: specs persist to <workspace>/.golem/graphs/<name>.json (0644, human-editable, git-friendly, names validated so a name cannot escape the directory; unreadable specs are surfaced in the catalog instead of hidden) and are re-read into the prompt catalog each turn with a 2s cache invalidated on save/delete. STILL OPEN: RunState. golem runs every turn in a throwaway ADK session (turn-<nano>), and workflow.RunState is reconstructed from session history, so a paused graph cannot resume across turns or restarts until graph runs get their own durable session.Service (in-memory for now, file/db backed next).

title: Enforce graph budgets at validate and run time
description: A graph is a licence to spawn agents in parallel. Without ceilings an agent-authored DAG is a self-DoS: unbounded nodes, unbounded depth, unbounded token spend.
design: Budgets: max_nodes, max_depth, max_concurrency, per-node timeout, wall_clock, token_spend. Validate-time checks reject over-budget specs before execution. Run-time enforcement: context deadline for wall clock, workflow.WithMaxConcurrency for width, node timeouts from NodeConfig.Timeout, and a token counter fed from the model callbacks that cancels the run when exceeded. On budget exhaustion the run stops with a clear, actionable error naming the exhausted budget and partial results are preserved.
acceptance_criteria: An over-budget spec is rejected at validate; a run that exceeds wall clock or token budget is cancelled and reports which budget was hit; concurrency never exceeds the configured ceiling (test with a counting node); partial results survive cancellation.
close_reason: Budgets mandatory and enforced at both ends: max_nodes/wall/tokens/concurrency bounds at validate time; at run time max_concurrency -> workflow.WithMaxConcurrency, a shared runBudget counts TotalTokenCount across every node (budgetModel refuses once the ceiling is passed, so one fan-out cannot multiply the ceiling), and the wall clock is checked before every model call plus on every event (breaking the range cancels in-flight nodes). Result reports tokens and per-node tokens/durations. Tests: fan-out token ceiling stops the run, expired deadline fails the call.

title: graph_* tools: validate, create, run, list, resume
description: The agent has no way to express or run a topology today - it can only call tools in a flat loop.
design: ADK functiontools registered on the primary agent alongside shell/hashline: graph_validate(spec), graph_create(spec) (validate then persist), graph_run(name, input), graph_list(), graph_resume(name, responses). graph_run returns a run id plus a summary of what executed; streaming node events reuse the existing StreamHandler path so the TUI and web already render progress. Tool descriptions must state the whitelist and budget ceilings so the model does not learn them by failing.
acceptance_criteria: Round trip works end to end from a prompt: agent writes a 3-node spec, validates, runs, and reports per-node outcomes; invalid spec returns a tool error naming the problem; graph_list shows persisted graphs; graph_resume continues a paused run.
notes:
LANDED (uncommitted): graph_list, graph_show, graph_validate, graph_save, graph_delete, graph_run (by name or inline spec) in pkg/graph/tools.go, wired into the primary agent in pkg/golem/agent.go (step 7b) and covered by TestAgentWiresGraphToolsAndSkill. graph_run returns the sink's output plus a per-node digest (tokens, duration, error); node events stream through dispatchGraphEvent so a fan-out renders as live rows in TUI/cockpit. graph_resume still open: it needs a durable ADK session (see golem-cfj.3).
Landed: graph_save/validate take the spec nested under a "spec" key (models reach for that shape); graph_run works by name or inline spec. Manager.Run now drives every run through its own runner (agent.New wrapping wf.Run + session.InMemoryService + AutoCreateSession) and deletes the session afterwards. That runner is required, not incidental: only a runner appends events to the session, the LLM flow rebuilds each request from session history, and a bare wf.RunNode call left node agents unable to see their own function responses (live run: 17 find_files/grep_files calls in 120s, nodes never finished). Regression test: TestNodeAgentSeesItsOwnToolResults. Also: tools.RepairArgs now rehydrates a JSON-encoded object/array in a string field and unwraps a one-element list around a string ({"tools":["read"]} -> "read"), both seen from live models. Wall-clock kills now name the nodes still running.

title: Agent-authored dynamic graphs on the ADK workflow engine
description:
google.golang.org/adk/v2@v2.5.0/workflow is already a dependency and golem barely uses it: agent.go:659 builds exactly one llmagent.New with a fixed toolset and runs it via runner.NewInMemory (:757). The engine gives nodes (AgentNode, FunctionNode, ToolNode, JoinNode, ParallelWorker), an EdgeBuilder with Add/AddFanOut/AddFanIn/AddRoute, per-node NodeConfig{ParallelWorker, RerunOnResume, WaitForOutput, RetryConfig, Timeout}, New(name, edges, WithMaxConcurrency, WithStateSchema), JSON-persisted RunState that survives across turns via Resume, HITL via NewRequestInputEvent/ResumeOrRequestInput, built-in validation (ErrNoStartNode, ErrNodesNotReachable, ErrUnconditionalCycle, ErrUnsupportedFanIn, ErrDuplicateNodeName) and NewDynamicNode for runtime-width scheduling.
So 'dynamic graph engineering' is really 'graph as data': a validated spec -> a runnable Workflow, exposed to the agent as tools.
design:
Spec is the source of truth, versioned ({"v":1}), JSON:
  {name, max_concurrency, nodes:[{id,kind,profile?,tools?}], edges:[[from,to,route?]], budgets:{max_nodes,depth,concurrency,wall_clock,tokens}}
Kinds whitelisted to agent|tool|join|parallel. FunctionNode and DynamicNode need Go closures and are rejected at validate time - that is the whole safety story for agent-authored graphs. Workflow objects are not round-trippable, so rebuild from spec on load.
Budgets are mandatory, not optional: an LLM writing a 200-node fan-out is a self-DoS.
workflow.New name uniqueness is per-session; two graphs sharing a name silently overwrite each other's RunState, so namespacing is enforced.
Swarm interaction (a graph node that is a swarm subagent) comes after the base lands.
acceptance_criteria: An agent can author a spec, have it validated with actionable errors, run it, and resume a paused run across turns; invalid graphs (cycle, unreachable node, duplicate name, disallowed kind, over-budget) are rejected before anything executes; run state survives a restart.

title: Graph spec schema and validator
description: Agent-authored graphs are untrusted input: they can request node kinds that need Go closures, unbounded fan-out, or cycles. ADK validates topology but knows nothing about our whitelist or budgets.
design: pkg/graph: Spec/Node/Edge/Budget types, Parse (strict JSON, unknown fields rejected), Validate -> []error with node ids in messages. Checks: schema version, whitelisted kinds, unique ids, no FunctionNode/DynamicNode, budgets present and within ceilings, then delegate topology to ADK's validation by building the Workflow and surfacing ErrNoStartNode/ErrNodesNotReachable/ErrUnconditionalCycle/ErrUnsupportedFanIn/ErrDuplicateNodeName with the offending id. Validation must be pure - no execution, no side effects.
acceptance_criteria: A table of valid and invalid specs; every rejection names the offending node or edge; valid specs build a Workflow without executing it; no code path can construct a FunctionNode or DynamicNode from a spec.
close_reason: pkg/graph/spec.go: versioned JSON spec (agent|tool|join, roles researcher/critic/coder/general, tool classes read/write/none), Validate returns every problem in one *ValidationError: name/id grammar, kind+role+field ownership, tool registry lookup, edge endpoints/duplicates/self-edges, reserved ids, exactly one sink, fan-in must land on a join, no routed edge into a join, no mixed routed/unrouted edges out of a node, reachability, cycle detection with the path, budget bounds, concurrency <= node count. Normalize fills defaults; WorkflowName() carries a shape hash so editing a graph does not inherit old run state. Tests: table of 25 rejection cases + multi-problem + fingerprint stability.

title: Confirmation gate via ADK toolconfirmation, rendered per transport
description: Nothing in pkg/ mentions toolconfirmation or any approval flow - every tool call, including from subagents and swarm peers, executes immediately. adk/v2/tool/toolconfirmation and the plugin Before/After tool hooks are available but unused.
design: Register the ADK toolconfirmation flow and have pkg/sandbox request confirmation for tools listed in RequireConfirm. One confirmation event, three renderings: TUI modal (reuse the existing modal viewport pattern), web prompt over the WS (with a resume-safe pending-approval state), and a no-op auto-deny for unattended contexts unless explicitly configured. Show the exact argv/patch being approved, not a summary. Deny returns a tool error.
acceptance_criteria: shell (or any tool in require_confirm) blocks until approved; the prompt shows the real command or diff; deny returns a tool error the model can route around rather than hanging or crashing; approval survives a transport reconnect; a subagent cannot approve on the user's behalf.
close_reason: Approval gate lands: pkg/approval + ADK toolconfirmation, TUI modal, web banner + /api/sessions/{id}/approval, readline prompt; subagents unattended (auto-deny); scripted-model round-trip test proves approve runs and refuse does not.

title: Real isolation: bwrap mode behind a flag
description: Policy alone cannot contain a hostile model - it is an in-process check that any tool bypass or shell escape defeats. Bubblewrap gives kernel-enforced isolation without root.
design: mode: bwrap wraps every shell invocation: bwrap --ro-bind / / --bind <workspace> <workspace> --dev /dev --proc /proc --tmpfs /tmp --unshare-net --die-with-parent --new-session -- bash -c <cmd>, with --unshare-net dropped when AllowNet is set. Detect bwrap at startup and fail closed (refuse bwrap mode) rather than silently degrading to policy mode. Container/podman is the documented escalation path, not part of this bead.
acceptance_criteria: In bwrap mode a command cannot write outside the workspace or read ~/.ssh (test asserts permission denied); network is unavailable unless AllowNet; missing bwrap refuses to start in bwrap mode with a clear error; policy mode is unchanged.
close_reason: implemented natively instead of wrapping bwrap: pkg/sandbox re-executes the golem binary as a Landlock shim (fs + TCP + signal scope, no root/namespaces/helper binary); mode isolation, config network/read_only, banner reports ABI, unsupported kernel is a startup error

title: Resume a session after reconnect instead of losing the stream
description: ui/src/lib/client.ts scheduleReconnect retries with 1.5^n backoff capped at 15s but reconnects stateless: anything streamed while the socket was down is lost, and on mobile the socket dies every time the browser backgrounds. (hub.go readPump already sets a 60s read deadline and refreshes it on pong, so half-open connections are reaped - the gap is purely the missing resume/backlog.)
design: Give every hub event a per-session monotonic seq. Server keeps a bounded ring buffer (e.g. 500 events) per session. Client remembers last_seq per session and sends {type:'resume', session_id, last_seq} immediately on open; server replays the gap or, if the gap is gone, tells the client to refetch full history. Add conn.SetReadDeadline + pong handler alongside the existing ping ticker, and a resume-failed fallback that refetches /api/sessions/{id}.
acceptance_criteria: Killing the WS (network drop) mid-stream and reconnecting delivers the missed tokens exactly once and in order; a gap larger than the buffer triggers a full refetch rather than a corrupt transcript; a dead peer is reaped within ~60s; tests cover replay, gap-overflow and ordering.
close_reason: Closed

title: feat(tui): attach images — clipboard paste hotkey, drag-drop paths, multimodal send
description:
## Problem
The TUI can only take text. There is no way to hand a screenshot to the model, which is the most natural debugging input there is (UI bugs, t212 charts, layout regressions).

## Terminal reality
Plain terminals never hand an app a clipboard image. Three routes, in order of reliability:

1. **Clipboard grab (works everywhere, incl. tmux)** — on a hotkey, run `wl-paste -t image/png` (Wayland) or `xclip -selection clipboard -t image/png -o` (X11), write to `$TMPDIR/golem-paste-<ts>.png`, attach. We read the clipboard ourselves, so tmux/terminal paste bindings are irrelevant.
2. **Path detection (drag & drop)** — most terminals drop a shell-escaped path into the input. If a token resolves to an existing image file (png/jpg/gif/webp), attach it and leave a `[image: shot.png]` chip in the input.
3. **Terminal paste protocols** (iTerm2/WezTerm `OSC 1337;File=...:base64` on Cmd+V) — bubbletea surfaces these as `KeyMsg{Runes:..., Paste:true}`; sniffable, but terminal-specific. Optional extra, not the MVP.

## Model path
- `pkg/golem/agent.go` builds input as `genai.Text(input)[0]`; adding `&genai.Part{InlineData: &genai.Blob{MIMEType, Data}}` is a small change.
- Native genai/ADK models (gemini-flash-latest = current default) are multimodal and accept it directly.
- `pkg/provider/openai/client.go convertRequest` flattens every part into `textBuilder`, so images are silently dropped for openai-compatible providers; needs `content` as a parts array with `image_url` data URLs. Only worth doing if the active provider/model is vision-capable.

## Memory
Fractal memory is JSONL text — bytes cannot persist. Store a stub event `[image #1: /tmp/golem-paste-1700.png 1440x900 212KB]` plus any model description, and send the actual blob only for the current turn.

## Display
No inline images under tmux (kitty/iterm graphics need passthrough and a cooperating terminal). Show a chip in the input box (`[img 1: 1440x900]`) and in the transcript card instead.

## Acceptance
- Hotkey grabs a clipboard image into a temp PNG and shows a chip; with no image in the clipboard it falls through to text paste.
- Dropped/typed image path attaches the same way.
- Attached image is sent as InlineData for vision models; a clear one-line error (and no silent drop) for text-only models/providers.
- Temp file is cleaned up on exit; nothing binary enters fractal memory.
- Tests: fake clipboard via injected `runClipboard` func, path-detection table test, agent-side part assembly test.
close_reason: Clipboard hotkey, dropped paths, multimodal send, image_url for OpenAI-compatible providers; tests + live pty verified

title: fix(tui): relayout on resize (re-wrap content, preserve reading position, fit the pane exactly)
description:
## Problem

Resizing the terminal / tmux pane (SIGWINCH → `tea.WindowSizeMsg`) only changed viewport
dimensions: the conversation stayed wrapped for the old width, the frame was 2 lines shorter
than the pane because the chrome heights were hard-coded (`headerHeight := 4`, `footerHeight := 6`),
and any re-render reset the reader's position.

## Fix

`Model.relayout()` now owns all layout:
- header and footer are measured with `lipgloss.Height`, so a wrapped header or a two-line
  status message can never push the frame past the pane height (tmux would scroll the screen);
- the markdown renderer is re-created at the new width, so the transcript re-wraps;
- reading position is preserved: pinned-to-newest stays pinned (the first pass lands on the
  end of the restored conversation), a scrolled-up reader keeps the same relative position.

## Verification

`TestModel_ResizeReflowsConversation`, `TestModel_ResizeKeepsReadingPosition`,
`TestModel_ViewFitsPane` (exact frame height across 5 sizes incl. a wrapping status line).
Mutation check: restoring the old fixed-height resize makes them fail
(`frame is 28 lines, must be exactly 30`). Real binary in a pty resized 120x30 → 70x18 repaints
an exactly 18-line frame, still pinned to the newest output, hints width-aware.
close_reason: Implemented and tested

title: Web search and fetch tools (Google CSE backend)
description: Add first-class web tools to Golem: web_search (query -> ranked results) and web_fetch (URL -> readable text). Search uses Google Programmable Search (CSE) behind a swappable SearchProvider interface; fetch is provider-independent with an SSRF guard and HTML->text extraction. Output is clipped head+tail and folds into fractal memory like any tool output; fetched content is treated as untrusted data.

title: validate: lowering the view budget may increase memory navigation

Measure against the real event log (per-task zoom/grep counts) before keeping this default; otherwise revert to 128/64 or make the smaller budget opt-in via config.

title: Swarm B: broadcast_message and send_message to unknown agents silently vanish (Subscribe never called)
description:
Live swarm testing shows messaging primitives are not wired for delivery:

1. NewToolset never calls Bus.Subscribe, so no agent ever subscribes to a channel. broadcast_message returns success but reaches nobody. (Subscribe in pkg/swarm/bus.go:167 has zero non-test call sites.)
2. Bus.Send returns nil even when the recipient has no mailbox: it creates the mailbox and delivers, but the message is only seen if the recipient calls check_inbox in the same run. A message to a finished/unknown agent disappears.
3. InvokeResult now carries SubagentID (Lane A), but a subagent finishes before the orchestrator can message it, so the id is only useful for messages sent DURING the subagent run.

Options to discuss: (a) have the orchestrator subscribe to channels and surface broadcasts via an unread-style nudge (like <swarm_inbox>); (b) route undeliverable mail to a dead-letter/DLQ the orchestrator is nudged about; (c) have subagents on the shared bus subscribe to 'orchestrator-directives' and drain at step boundaries; (d) make send to an unknown agent return an explicit warning. Part of Swarm lane B.
close_reason: Fixed by lane B delivery guarantees. (a) The orchestrator + every subagent now Register on the bus (NewToolsetWithSession), so broadcast_message fans out to all live agents' mailboxes -- no Subscribe needed -- and the <swarm_inbox> nudge surfaces unread broadcasts. (b) send_message to an unknown/offline agent is detected: Bus.Send returns DeliveryDeadLetter, parks the message in a bounded dead-letter queue, and the tool tells the sender 'could NOT be delivered ... registered agents are: [...].' (c) Subagents register for the lifetime of their run and unregister at the end; the orchestrator sees peer ids via the invoke_subagent header. See golem-c8y.

title: perf(tui): bound startup replay to a tail slice instead of copying the whole log
description: NewModel calls store.EventsSlice(0, store.CountEvents()) which copies every event into memory on every startup, even though only the last 5 turns are shown. On a large store (tens of thousands of events) this is an O(N) allocation and copy before the TUI paints. Add a bounded tail accessor (e.g. Store.EventsTail(n)) and have NewModel use it. Found in the golem-sma.3 review.
acceptance_criteria: Startup replay reads only the tail window from the store; no full-log copy; a test covers the tail accessor at the boundaries.
close_reason: Added Store.EventsTail(n) and NewModel now reads only the last 500 events instead of copying the whole log. Test: TestStoreEventsTail covers n>len, n=0, n<0.

title: fix(tui): replayed tools must not show as RUNNING
description: eventsToEntries marks a tool entry IsRunning=true and only clears it when the following echo is in the window. If the tail window ends on a tool whose echo never arrived (e.g. a turn interrupted mid-tool, or the event cap splitting a pair), the replay renders a ghost RUNNING tool card in historical output. Force every replayed tool to a terminal state after building the entries. Found in the golem-sma.3 review.
acceptance_criteria: A tool event with no matching echo in the replay window renders as finished, not running; a test covers a trailing unpaired tool.
close_reason: eventsToEntries now forces every replayed tool to a terminal state, so an interrupted/pair-split tool cannot replay as RUNNING. Test: TestEventsToEntriesTrailingToolNotRunning.

title: fix(memory): catch up the persisted view instead of full rebuild on TailTo mismatch
description: loadStateLocked (pkg/memory/fractal/view.go) rejects the saved tiling whenever saved TailTo != total - LiveHeadCount, which is exactly the crash case: events appended after the last view save. It then falls back to a full Rebuild, re-coarsening detail and defeating the persistence goal. Fix: when saved TailTo < expected, load the saved tiling and append level-0 parts for [savedTail, expectedTail) then re-fit, instead of rebuilding from 0. Rebuild only when the saved tiling is geometrically invalid or saved TailTo > expected.
acceptance_criteria: A store with a saved view behind by N events loads and catches up to the current tail without a full Rebuild; a test covers it.
close_reason: loadStateLocked now loads a saved tiling whose TailTo lags the store and catches it up with level-0 parts + re-fit instead of a full rebuild; Rebuild only when the tiling is invalid or extends past the tail. Added TestViewCatchesUpPersistedTiling.

title: fix(memory): bound node size if the summarizer never converges
description: SummarizeBounded (pkg/memory/fractal/compactor.go) removed the previous truncateUTF8 hard cap. If the compactor model returns an over-length line on all maxSummaryCorrections attempts, the oversized node is stored as-is, and Render/calculateSizeBytes then carry an arbitrarily large line (prompt bloat). OptChat tolerates a few bytes over 512, not 100x. Fix: add a generous last-resort safety cap (e.g. 4x DefaultNodeTargetBytes) applied only after the retry loop is exhausted, and surface a signal (log or memory stat) when it triggers.
acceptance_criteria: A summarizer that always returns a huge line yields a stored node within the safety cap, and the cap event is visible (not silent).
close_reason: SummarizeBounded now caps at maxNodeBytes (4x target) after the correction loop and logs when it triggers, so a non-converging model cannot store an unbounded node. Added TestSummarizeBoundedCapsNonConverging.

title: test(review): make the view-persistence test actually prove loading
description: TestViewPersistsAcrossRestart (pkg/memory/fractal/view_test.go) asserts the rendered view is equal before and after reopen, but Rebuild is deterministic given the same nodes and config, so an identical tiling is expected even if load never ran. The test cannot fail if persistence regresses to a rebuild. Fix: before NewView, call store.SaveViewState with a valid-but-non-rebuild tiling (e.g. 16 level-1 parts over tail 32 where a rebuild would produce 32 level-0 parts) and assert NewView returns exactly that tiling. Found during the golem-sid.7 review.
acceptance_criteria: The test fails if NewView rebuilds instead of loading, and passes with load.
close_reason: Added TestViewLoadsPersistedTilingNotRebuild: injects a valid non-rebuild tiling (16 level-1 parts) and asserts NewView returns exactly it, so the test fails if persistence regresses to a rebuild.

title: fix(memory): retry over-length summaries instead of truncating and correct the 512-byte ruler
description: Summarizers silently truncate to 512 bytes (compactor.go:80,146) via truncateUTF8, dropping the tail of long summaries. The prompt claims the reference ruler is exactly 512 bytes; it measures 505 (compactor.go:26). The spec says to resend a Too long correction up to 5 times and keep the shortest line.
design: Enforce length with a retry wrapper around the Summarizer contract (or inside Compactor.BuildNode) that appends the Too long correction and re-calls. Fix the ruler constant to exactly 512 bytes.
acceptance_criteria: A too-long summary triggers a correction follow-up up to 5 times, keeping the shortest candidate; a fake summarizer test proves the retry path and that no stored node is silently clipped. A test asserts len(ScaleLine512Bytes) == 512. -race passes.
close_reason: Summarizers no longer truncate: added CorrectingSummarizer + SummarizeBounded which resends the Too long correction up to 5 times and keeps the shortest candidate; BuildNode uses it. Ruler now exactly 512 bytes. Added TestScaleLineIsExactly512Bytes and TestSummarizeBoundedCorrectsOverLength. Full go test -race ./... green.

title: Swarm B: make it an actual swarm (async delegation, enforced locks, lock events)
description: Lane B epic. Current swarm is mechanism-only and sequential. Sub-items: (1) async/parallel invoke_subagent fan-out + join instead of blocking functiontool; (2) enforce advisory locks inside hashline_patch/write_file/shell via ListLocks; (3) emit WSEventSwarmLock (currently defined but never emitted) and show locks in the cockpit; (4) per-subagent lifecycle on the bus; (5) populate Message.SessionID/Metadata; (6) consistent Broadcast semantics (channel handlers run inline/blocking while global listeners run async); (7) delivery guarantees — Send auto-creates mailboxes so messages to dead agents vanish silently, add ack/undeliverable handling. Do after lane A proves the value.
close_reason: Swarm lane B shipped. (1) Fan-out: ADK v2.5.0 platform.RunTasks already runs parallel tool calls concurrently with a completion barrier, so multiple invoke_subagent calls in one turn are a real fan-out+join. (2) Locks enforced at the edit layer: pkg/swarm/locks.go CheckToolLock refuses write_file/replace_regex/hashline_patch when another owner holds the resource; wired into the orchestrator BeforeToolCallback (pkg/golem/agent.go) and the subagent BeforeToolCallbacks (pkg/subagent/runner.go). ADK skips tool.Run and surfaces {error} so enforcement is real. (3) Lock events: Bus.OnLockChange -> WSEventSwarmLock in session_manager (both CreateSession paths, unsub on delete/close); UI Locks tab in SwarmTree.svelte + swarmLocks store. (4) Per-subagent lifecycle: NewToolsetWithSession registers the agent (+mailbox) and Runner defers Unregister; orchestrator registers as swarm.OrchestratorID. (5) Message.SessionID populated from toolset session. (6) Broadcast now fans to every registered agent's mailbox + safeCall channel handlers + async global listeners; returns delivery count. (7) Delivery guarantees: registered-agent registry, Send returns DeliveryStatus (delivered/dead_letter), bounded DLQ + dead-letter count, sender warned on undeliverable send. Tests: TestSwarmBusRegistryAndDeadLetter, TestSwarmBroadcastReachesUnsubscribedRegisteredAgents, TestSwarmLockEvents, TestCheckToolLock, TestToolsetRegistrationLifecycle. build/vet/race green, UI builds.

title: DefaultPath ignores $GOLEM_CONFIG_DIR when ~/.config/golem/config.json exists
description:
pkg/config/config.go:148 DefaultPath calls UserDir() (which honours $GOLEM_CONFIG_DIR first) but then, if that dir has no config.json, falls back to an existing ~/.config/golem/config.json before returning the UserDir path. So with GOLEM_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/scratch and a real ~/.config/golem/config.json present, DefaultPath returns the real file and any write goes to it.
Found while smoke-testing web token generation: a run with GOLEM_CONFIG_DIR pointed at a temp dir wrote its token into the user's real config. Harmless there, but an explicit env var should not lose to a hardcoded fallback.
design: When $GOLEM_CONFIG_DIR is set, it should be authoritative: return its config.json whether or not the file exists yet, and skip the ~/.config/golem fallback. Keep the fallback only for the no-env-var case, and document the precedence in the UserDir doc comment.
acceptance_criteria: With $GOLEM_CONFIG_DIR set, DefaultPath returns $GOLEM_CONFIG_DIR/config.json even when the file does not exist and ~/.config/golem/config.json does; unset behaviour is unchanged; a test covers both cases.

title: Decide: should TUI and web share sessions?
description: Today they cannot: the TUI owns an in-process agent, the web cockpit owns a runtime.SessionManager, and pkg/swarm is in-process only, so a TUI and a -serve instance are separate swarms that cannot see each other. Once pkg/runtime exists this becomes a real choice rather than an accident.
design: Two shapes: (a) independent - TUI keeps its own sessions, web keeps its own, simple, no shared state, two places to look; (b) TUI as a WS client of -serve - one runtime, both surfaces see the same sessions and the same swarm, but the TUI stops working when the server is down and needs offline/attach semantics. Prototype (b) behind a flag (-attach <url>) and measure the ergonomics before committing. Note the same decision applies to any future chat transport.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision with the trade-offs, plus a working spike of the chosen shape (or a spike of both) demonstrating attach to a running server, seeing its sessions, and surviving a server restart.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lazy load and idle-suspend sessions to respect the single-writer store
description: bbolt allows one writer per file with a 5s open timeout (store.go:81). Holding N open sessions means N open databases and N compactor goroutines, and a second process on the same memory dir fails.
design: Open a session's store on first activation, suspend it after an idle window (configurable, default ~5 min) keeping its transcript in memory for instant re-display, and hard-cap concurrently open stores (e.g. 3) with LRU suspension. Compactor workers stop on suspend. Surface the state in the header (open vs suspended) so the behaviour is not mysterious.
acceptance_criteria: With 10 sessions created only the cap are open at any time; a suspended session reactivates without visible reload delay; no bbolt lock contention after idle suspend; compactor goroutines do not leak (goroutine count returns to baseline after suspension).
close_reason: Extracted SessionManager into pkg/runtime with Suspend/Resume, LRU open-store cap, and idle suspension; all pkg/server and pkg/runtime tests pass

title: Visualise graphs: TUI modal and web DAG view with live node status
description: A topology the user cannot see is a topology they cannot trust. TUI already has modal viewports and a minimap; the web UI has a SwarmTree component to model on.
design: TUI: /graph modal listing graphs, then a lipgloss DAG/tree render with per-node state (pending/running/ok/failed), elapsed time and the exhausted-budget marker; reuse the model-picker modal pattern (viewport + selection + Enter) and the live node events already flowing through StreamHandler. Web: a DAG panel next to SwarmTree fed by the same node events over WS. Read-only in v1 - editing topology in a UI is a separate, later bead.
acceptance_criteria: While a graph runs the user can see which node is executing and which have completed; a failed node is visually distinct and names its error; the view works for a 12-node graph without overflowing either surface; no rendering when no graph has run.
close_reason: Closed

title: Audit log of every tool decision
description: Once tools can be denied or require approval there is no record of what was asked, what was decided, or what ran.
design: Append-only JSONL in the memory dir (audit.jsonl): timestamp, session id, tool, sanitised args, verdict, reason, duration, exit code. Reuse the fractal store's append discipline. Include denials and confirmations, not just executions. Never log secrets - run args through the same redaction as the env allowlist.
acceptance_criteria: Every allow, deny and confirm produces exactly one audit record; records are valid JSONL and survive a restart; no secret value appears in the log (test with a planted token).
close_reason: Decision log: pkg/approval/audit.go (ring + JSONL 0600), recorded at the Gate choke point for allow/deny/confirm plus the human answer; /audit in the TUI, GET /api/sandbox/audit; sandbox.audit path, banner line.

title: Throttle token rendering on mobile
description: Every WS token event triggers a store update and a markdown re-render of the streaming message. Fine on a desktop, visibly janky on a phone during a long reply.
design: Coalesce tokens client-side into ~30fps frames (or batch by time+size) before touching the store; render the streaming message as plain text and only run the markdown pipeline on completion; measure first with a long reply on a throttled CPU profile before adding complexity.
acceptance_criteria: A 5k-token reply on a throttled mobile profile stays interactive (no long tasks >50ms attributable to markdown); final rendered output identical to today; no dropped or reordered text.
close_reason: Closed

title: polish(web): registered-but-unconfigured search, DNS check strictness, missing content-type
description: From the golem-1mr.5 review (the API-key leak in search errors was fixed inline with redactSecret): (1) web_search is always registered even when unconfigured, so the model may repeatedly call it and get a not-configured message - consider registering only when key+cx are present; (2) ensurePublicHost rejects when ANY resolved IP is private while the dialer would accept a public one - align or document; (3) a response with no Content-Type is treated as textual, so a binary body could be imported as garbage.

title: polish(importer): open the DB read-only for format deduction and make discovery tests hermetic
description: Two items from the golem-2hp.3 review: (1) deduceFileFormat opens the SQLite file read-write just to inspect sqlite_master; open it mode=ro like the parser does. (2) TestDiscoverHistories is not hermetic - it now picks up the host OpenCode/Cursor sessions; set HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME to a temp dir like cli_test does, or assert by ID.
close_reason: Format deduction now opens SQLite read-only (deduce uses openSQLiteReadOnly, shared with the parser) so deducing never creates or touches a DB file; TestDiscoverHistories is hermetic (HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME/APPDATA/OPENCODE_DB_PATH point at a temp dir) and asserts exactly the two fixture sessions instead of 'at least 2'.

title: fix(agent): make clipHeadTail rune-safe
description: clipHeadTail cuts at byte offsets, so a multi-byte rune at the head/tail boundary can be split into invalid UTF-8. Use the existing TruncateUTF8-style rune-safe cut for both ends. Also the marker pushes the result ~22 bytes over the nominal 30000; acceptable but worth stating.
close_reason: clipHeadTail keeps its budget and stays valid UTF-8: both copies (pkg/golem tool clip, pkg/web fetch clip) cut on rune boundaries, count the truncation marker against the limit, and fall back to a bare head when the limit is smaller than the marker; tests cover 2/3/4-byte runes in both packages

title: deferred: wait for summarization so no placeholders reach the model
description: Thesis section 6: a turn waits until every prior message is summarized. Golem renders immediately and can show (not summarized yet). Deferred: a synchronous pre-turn build risks adding latency; placeholders are rare because the post-turn Pump builds the tail. Revisit if observed.
close_reason: Deferred by design, not forgotten: a synchronous pre-turn build would put a provider round-trip on the critical path of every turn to avoid a placeholder that the post-turn Pump already makes rare. Placeholders are honest to the model ('not summarized yet: zoom it'), and compaction views no longer contain any (golem-01i.11 renders built lines only). Revisit only if placeholders are actually observed in a turn view.

title: fix(compactor): join short lines with a newline, not semicolon
description: Thesis section 2: two short lines are joined by a newline. compactor.go uses "; ". Switch to newline (Render already replaces newlines with spaces).
close_reason: Short lines merge with a newline; Test: TestFreeMergeJoinsWithNewline.

title: cleanup: CompactorConfig.Concurrency is dead (Pump is sequential)
description: Concurrency is stored and defaulted but Pump builds nodes sequentially with no worker pool, so the golem-nbk.5 change from 4 to 2 does nothing. Either implement parallel node building (bounded by Concurrency) or remove/deprecate the field so it does not imply contention control that does not exist.
close_reason: Removed CompactorConfig.Concurrency: Pump walks levels in watermark order (a parent only after its children) and runs one compaction call at a time, so the field implied contention control that never existed. The struct doc now states why there is no concurrency knob; nothing else read the field.

title: polish: retry gaps (HTTP 408) and re-streamed partials
description: Two low-priority gaps from the golem-nbk.6 review: (1) doRequestWithRetry omits 408 Request Timeout and isTransientError does not match a bare api error 408, so a request-timeout status is retried at neither layer - add 408 to retryableStatus; (2) a transient error with zero tool calls still restarts the turn and re-streams any partial text already sent to the handler, which the TUI can show twice - only restart when no output has been streamed.
close_reason: Both review gaps closed: 408 Request Timeout is retryable at the provider (retryableStatus) and matched by isTransientError (plus 'request timeout'), with a client test that a 408 is retried once; and a turn is only restarted when nothing has been streamed (shouldRestartTurn now takes streamedBytes), so partial text is never rendered twice — table test covers the streamed case

title: fix(agent): avoid live-head duplication mid-turn
description: buildInstruction (pkg/golem/agent.go) drops the in-flight user event only when it is the newest event. Within a single turn that makes several model calls (tool use), later calls see the turn user message both in the runner conversation history and in the live head. Low impact, but wasteful and potentially confusing. Document the behavior or suppress the current turn user event for all calls in the turn.
acceptance_criteria: Either documented in code, or the turn user message does not appear in the live head on any model call within the turn.
close_reason: Agent now tracks the in-flight turn user event ID; the InstructionProvider excludes it from the live head on every model call of the turn (not just when newest). Added exclusion-filter assertions to the live-head tests.

title: chore(agent): dedupe duplicated swarm memory line in the system prompt
description: agent.go:557-558 repeats the sentence Both you and your subagents share the same fractal memory store. twice, introduced by the uncommitted swarm change.
design: Delete the duplicate line.
acceptance_criteria: The sentence appears once; no other prompt text changes.
close_reason: Removed the duplicated subagent-shared-memory line from the system prompt.

title: note(importer): stream large OpenCode sessions instead of buffering
description: ParseOpenCode loads all messages for a session and all parts for each message into memory before returning. Fine for typical sessions but unbounded for a very large one. Consider streaming events (or appending as parsed) if a giant session is encountered.
close_reason: Documented rather than restructured: the part query is per message, so ParseOpenCode peaks at the largest single message, and the real cost is the memory write that follows. A streaming callback would change every importer's signature for a case not yet seen; the comment on ParseOpenCode records the trade-off and the trigger to revisit.

title: polish(compactor): view-ends-at-node and persisted Pump watermarks
description: Two nuances from the golem-01i.8 review: (1) RenderCompacted does not implement the thesis rule that a compaction view ends at the node and holds only built lines - it compacts the whole current view and can exceed the target when no parent is built; (2) Pump level watermarks reset on restart, so the first pass after a restart still scans the whole tree once. Persist the watermarks (or accept and document the one-time scan).
close_reason: RenderCompactedEndingAt: a node's compaction view now ends where the node starts and holds only built lines (straddling parts are split back into children; unmeetable targets leave the view long instead of padding it with placeholders) — BuildNode passes index<<level; Pump watermarks persist under the view bucket so a restart resumes instead of rescanning (node writes commit before the watermark that covers them); tests: view ending/splitting/placeholder-free, watermarks survive restart

title: polish(tui): startup replay nits (input-history bound, tool exit code, display width)
description: From the golem-sma.7 review, non-blocking nits: (1) inputHistory is now derived from the same 500-event tail as the replay, so very old prompts drop out of up-arrow recall - document or give it its own limit; (2) a replayed tool whose echo is missing shows EXIT 0 because the echo text carries no exit code - consider a neutral status; (3) clampLines truncates by rune count, not terminal display width, so wide CJK/emoji paths can still overflow the header.
close_reason: All three review nits closed: up-arrow recall has its own bound (inputHistoryMaxEntries=100, built by buildInputHistory, documented as reading the startup scan window); a replayed tool with no echo shows a neutral 'EXIT ?' instead of a false EXIT 0 (ExitCodeUnknown + eventsToEntries marks unpaired calls); clampLines measures display width via lipgloss so CJK/emoji paths cannot overflow the header. Tests cover each.

title: polish(tui): width-aware startup header and timestamp guard
description: The header renders the workspace path verbatim through HeaderTitleStyle and is not wrapped or truncated, so a deep path can overflow the block; formatStartupHeader also renders a degenerate/zero event timestamp as a huge Nd ago. Truncate the path to the viewport width and guard last-active when the timestamp is zero. Found in the golem-sma.3 review.
acceptance_criteria: The header fits the viewport width and a zero timestamp does not render an absurd age.
close_reason: Added clampLines (rune-safe, ellipsis) applied to the header at viewport width, and a zero-timestamp guard that omits the age. Tests: TestClampLines, TestFormatStartupHeaderZeroTimestamp.

title: chore(review): share the UTF-8 truncate helper and test low-water normalization
description: Nit 1: truncateSafe (pkg/golem/agent.go) and truncateUTF8 (pkg/memory/fractal/compactor.go) are near-identical; export one from fractal and reuse. Nit 2: NewView normalization sets LowWaterBytes = ViewBudgetBytes/2, but tiny high-water values (ViewBudgetBytes=1) yield low=0 and this path is untested. Add a test and clamp low to at least 1 where sensible. Found during the golem-sid.7 review.
acceptance_criteria: One truncate helper; a test covers ViewConfig normalization including tiny high-water values.
close_reason: Exported fractal.TruncateUTF8 and removed the duplicate truncateSafe; added TestNewViewNormalizesWaterMarks and clamped low-water to >=1 for tiny high-water values.
